title: literary-translator profile.yml
description: Structural contract for .claude/literary-translator/profile.yml. Shape/type/enum/conditional validation only -- filesystem existence, path-traversal safety, and placeholder-substring rejection are procedural checks done by profile_validate.py, not this schema.

conservation.description: Opt-in (#196/#202 content-conservation gate, validate_conservation.py). Absent -- the common case, most projects are not a hand-wrap -- means the wrapper-conservation check is a documented SKIP, never a forced-on hard gate. Only declare this for a source hand-wrapped into this project's format from some other pre-wrap form (e.g. pdftotext -layout output split into an EPUB by hand), where the exact pre-wrap text has been preserved as an immutable baseline. All three paths are durable-root-relative (no absolute path, no '..' segment -- path-traversal safety, checked procedurally by validate_conservation.py, not this schema).

baseline_path.description: The exact pre-wrap source text the wrap was made from, preserved verbatim.

provenance_path.description: JSON map, built at wrap time, of baseline character spans -> manifest block_id -- see validate_conservation.py's own module docstring for the exact shape.

allowed_omissions_path.description: Optional JSON file of line-regexes and half-open CHARACTER-offset (Unicode code point, never UTF-8 byte) ranges (front matter, running heads, page numbers) the coverage-gap check tolerates as legitimately un-provenanced. Same coordinate system as provenance_path's baseline_start/baseline_end -- do not compute these with a byte-counting tool (wc -c, grep -b) for a non-ASCII baseline. Absent -- everything in the baseline must be provenance-covered.

effort.description: Reasoning effort threaded to codex (mass translate/review + glossary passes) and to the Claude fix step. Excludes 'none'/'minimal' (nonsensical for accuracy work) and 'max' (codex-companion's --effort flag throws on it).

max_codex_jobs_per_batch.description: #409 stage 0. OPTIONAL -- a worst-case CODEX-JOB-COUNT preflight cap for mass-translate, independent of batch_agent_cap above (which estimates Workflow agent() calls; this estimates real codex dispatches). Per segment: 1 translate job + (max_fix_rounds + 1) review jobs = max_fix_rounds + 2 -- EXACT for mass-translate-wf.template.js, whose review retry re-reads the artifact codex already wrote rather than starting a second job, and a FLOOR for segment_dispatch_driver.py, which may additionally spend one fabricated-loc re-review per segment (hard-capped at one, so max_fix_rounds + 3 per invocation on that path). The fix rounds are NOT codex jobs -- the fix step is a plain Workflow agent() call, never a codex_job.py launch. Deliberately NOT required (unlike batch_agent_cap): many existing profiles/fixtures predate this knob and must stay valid without it. #735: this is a preflight cap and nothing else -- it reaches no agent prompt and no translation, review or ledger artifact; it appears only as run diagnostics -- the preflight's own refusal result, the driver's session journal, and `engine.max_codex_jobs_per_batch` on every successful driver result -- so it is deliberately absent from resume_setup.py's DIGEST_SUBST_FIELDS. Changing it mid-book mints NO fresh RUN_ID and discards no draft in flight, which is what makes it usable as the runaway backstop it is meant to be rather than a number that has to be got right before the book's real shape is known. batch_agent_cap beside it is still hashed, so changing THAT still mints a fresh RUN_ID and retranslates the drafts in flight it orphans.

model.description: Optional codex model id threaded to the W5 codex dispatch (mass translate/review only; not the glossary or fix paths). Unset (the common case) means codex resolves its own ~/.codex config default.

enabled.description: Master switch for the W3 glossary/canon RESEARCH pass. When false, W3 still runs the mandatory language smoke test (W3a's segpack.py re-runs that same extractor over every segment and W5 acts on its new_names, so name detection stays load-bearing), but skips glossary_batch_plan.py, resume_setup.py, the glossary Workflow, the canon merge, and the skeptic pass; it bootstraps an empty, fully stamped canon.json with canon_validate.py --init and rejoins at the mandatory homonym-split evidence gate exactly as the no_new_candidates SKIP branch does. An existing canon.json is NOT discarded -- --init is create-only, so its entries keep reaching every segpack. Absent means true, so every existing profile keeps validating unchanged. Outside compute_profile_semantics_hash()'s named-six allowlist (cache_key.py:532), so adding or flipping this key never re-translates a converged segment on its own -- but enabling it later and canonizing names does change affected segments' used_terms_hash and makes them dispatch-eligible again. Adding this property to profile.schema.json itself moves resume_setup.py's own _schemas_dir_hash() (it hashes every top-level *.schema.json file's raw bytes under durable_root/schemas/ into input_digest), so the FIRST Step 0a refresh after this release is a one-time resume-identity reset: any in-flight mass-translate or glossary run cannot resume across it -- it starts a fresh run_id and re-dispatches from scratch, including any partial glossary batch.

citation_content_types.description: 1.16.1 (#347). Content-Type prefixes fetch_citation.py may admit for a cited source, substituted into glossary-pass-wf as {{CITATION_CONTENT_TYPES}}. An empty array (or an absent key) means the fetcher's shipped default: text/, application/xhtml, application/xml, application/json. Set it only when THIS corpus cites something the default excludes -- scanned archives are the motivating case. Each entry is a bare type/subtype PREFIX matched with startswith, so parameters, wildcards and uppercase are rejected here rather than being silently ignored downstream. The trailing (?![\s\S]) is a true end-of-string anchor, NOT decoration: jsonschema evaluates `pattern` with Python's `re`, whose `$` also matches before a trailing newline, so `...$` would admit "text/pdf\n" here while fetch_citation.py's own \Z-anchored copy refuses it -- a preflight gate that disagrees with the runtime gate is worse than no preflight gate. A parity test pins all three copies together.

skeptic_pass.description: RFC #215 Phase 2 structural-risk triage + adverse-only skeptic pass. OPT-IN and ADVISORY in 1.6.0 (disabled by default; the warn->block flip is deferred to Phase 3). When enabled, the W-step runs suspicion_scan.py -> skeptic_setup.py -> skeptic-pass-wf -> skeptic_report.py; the category-5 audit gate is unchanged and skeptic_report.py is a separate advisory command. This object is OUTSIDE profile_semantics_hash's allowlist, so adding/setting it never re-translates a converged segment. The `default:` values below MIRROR skeptic_constants.py's *_DEFAULT constants (profile_validate.py does not materialize schema defaults, so the constants are the real runtime defaults; a parity test asserts no drift). An enabled profile passes these as explicit CLI overrides via the W-step.

enabled.description: Master switch. When false (default) the skeptic W-step is skipped entirely and no existing output changes.

windows_per_entity.description: Max whole-block citable windows fed to the skeptic per entity; exceeding it sets windows_truncated so the skeptic may honestly return insufficient_window/escalate.

sample_cap.description: GLOBAL total for the `sampled` risk class (largest-remainder across category strata), not per-stratum. The strata are category-only: the sample never reads an entry's model-authored `confidence` (#506).

dispersion_threshold.description: `high_dispersion` fires when an entity's distinct-seg occurrence count reaches this.

near_cap.description: `near_merge` emits at most this many top pairs.

near_pair_budget.description: `near_merge` pre-enumeration materialization budget; exceeding it truncates deterministically WITH a logged annotation (never silent).

citation_block_types.description: Override the block `type` tags that count as citation for `all_citation`. Omit to use the per-source.format default (gutenberg_epub/plain_text -> FN,QUOTE; custom/unknown -> all_citation DISABLED fail-safe).

forbidden_patterns.description: OPT-IN, default absent (#520). A project's own deterministic, codepoint-decidable style bans, which the plugin ships NO defaults for -- the style contract lives in the project's style_bible.md and only the project knows which of its rules are mechanically decidable. Each entry is a Python `re` pattern tested by final_audit.py's WARN 5 against every string leaf of a converged draft's blocks/footnotes/verses, EXACTLY as the translator wrote it: sentinels are not stripped, markdown emphasis is not stripped, and no normalization is applied to the scanned text. Purely ADVISORY -- a hit is one WARN line, never a hard failure and never an exit-code change. A pattern that fails to compile is reported as its own WARN naming the id, never silently skipped, so an unenforced rule cannot read as a clean run -- that is the one rejection final_audit.py owns, because it is the only one THIS schema cannot make. Every question about SHAPE is settled here, at Step 0. The list is not size-capped and the patterns are not cost-bounded: profile.yml is operator-authored, the same trust footing on which validate_conservation.py already compiles operator-supplied line_patterns.

id.description: Stable slug naming the rule, echoed in the WARN line so an operator can trace it back to the style_bible clause it enforces. The trailing (?![\s\S]) is a true end-of-string anchor, NOT decoration -- same pitfall the citation_content_types pattern above documents: jsonschema evaluates `pattern` with Python's `re`, whose `$` also matches before a trailing newline, so `...$` would admit "rule\n" here. That id is then interpolated into the declaration WARN, where it is not covered by the whole-line normalization the HIT warnings get.

pattern.description: Python `re` pattern. Matched with finditer, so the reported hit count is over NON-OVERLAPPING matches.

message.description: What the operator should do about a hit. CR/LF are deliberately NOT forbidden here: PyYAML loads a folded `>` scalar with a trailing newline and a literal `|` scalar with its breaks intact, so a prohibition would refuse ordinary block authoring at Step 0. final_audit.py normalizes the whole emitted WARN line instead.

terms.description: OPT-IN, default absent (#199). A project's own pinned COMMON-NOUN terms of art -- an office title, a recurring institutional realia -- that must render one way for the whole book. canon.json cannot hold such a term (it is a proper-name dictionary by construction, and the shipped adjudication contract never accepts an is_proper_name:false entry), and final_audit.py's cross-segment glossary-diff keys on canon entries and per-draft names[], both proper-name channels -- so without this a recurring common noun renders two ways in one delivered volume and nothing reports it. This declares the DETECTION half only; the term itself is pinned where it always was, in style_bible.md section C's title/honorific mapping, which is delivered in full to every translate and review job. final_audit.py's WARN 6 reports a CARRIER (a block, a footnote definition, or ONE delivered verse field) whose source contains source_form MORE OFTEN than its own translated counterpart contains target_form. The count is per carrier, and a verse's rendered and literal_gloss are separate carriers, so one correct occurrence can never mask a drifted one beside it. Purely ADVISORY -- never a hard failure, never an exit-code change -- and the run always prints how many terms it checked, so an absent or empty list cannot read as a clean pass. Matching is by SUBSTRING over NFC-normalized, casefolded text, which is what makes a suffixing target language work: pin the INVARIANT part of the target form and its inflected surfaces are found inside it. A target language that inflects by prefix or stem change cannot be pinned this way. Carriers the active policy passes through UNTRANSLATED are never compared: footnote definitions under footnotes.apparatus_policy preserve_source, verses under verse_policy.mode skip, and the placeholder-only draft block of a mount:"block" verse. The list is not size-capped: profile.yml is operator-authored, the same trust footing as forbidden_patterns above.

source_form.description: The source-language term to look for in a carrier's own source text. Deliberately no id and no message field: unlike a forbidden_patterns regex, this string is readable on its own and is echoed verbatim in the WARN line, so a separate identifier would name what is already named.

target_form.description: The frozen target-language rendering, or the INVARIANT part of it (a stem) when the target language inflects by suffix. A carrier translating source_form without containing this string is what WARN 6 reports.

admit_contract_only_stale.description: OPT-IN, default false (#533). When true, the whole-project completeness gate (final_audit.py) and the assembly gate (assemble.py) admit an already-converged unit that went 'stale' ONLY because style_contract_hash moved -- a style-bible edit inside the STYLE_CONTRACT markers -- provided its .ever_converged sentinel is not absent, its on-disk draft still matches the recorded reviewed_draft_sha1, and every other moved cache-key field is machinery-only. This makes the tooling agree with the shipped rule R9 ('a style-contract edit applies FORWARD; a converged segment stays converged'), which the gates otherwise contradict by refusing to ship until every flipped unit is reviewed again. It does NOT widen SAFE_STALE_CARVEOUT_FIELDS, rewrite any ledger record or stamp any hash: the record keeps saying 'stale' and every admitted segment is named on stderr and in the run's structured stdout, so shipping them is a recorded operator act. It CANNOT distinguish a contract ADDITION from a contract REVERSAL -- a reversed rule genuinely demanded the defect in the earlier segments -- which is why it is a declaration and not a default. Only a literal true enables it; absent, null and false all mean refuse. Keep the value stable from W7 through delivery: every gate reads this same field, and toggling it mid-chain makes them disagree.

conservation_hollow_floor.description: Optional thresholds for validate_conservation.py's output-coverage v1 floor (#202, WARN-only): a block is flagged hollowed_output_block when its source word count is >= min_source_words AND its output word count is <= max_output_words. Absent -- both default (1, 0), i.e. 'non-empty source, empty output'. Absolute word counts, deliberately not a ratio -- see validate_assembled.py's own docstring on why a length-band is unsound across language pairs. A within-cohort ratio-based surfacer now exists alongside this floor as the separate, opt-in conservation_ratio_band block below (#202 R3, PARTIAL): it compares a block only against its own cohort's measured distribution, never a cross-language absolute band, and is structurally unable to catch uniform cohort-wide truncation -- see validate_conservation.py's own module docstring.

conservation_ratio_band.description: Optional config for validate_conservation.py's output-coverage within-cohort ratio-outlier surfacer (#202 R3, PARTIAL -- WARN-only, does NOT close #202). OPT-IN: absent or null means this lane does not run at all and output-coverage behaves exactly as in 1.11.0. Blocks are grouped into cohorts by their raw manifest block type and a block is compared only against its OWN cohort's measured out/source word-ratio distribution -- never a cross-language-pair or project-wide absolute threshold (that shape is refused, see validate_conservation.py's own module docstring). min_source_words_band (default 40) is a per-block eligibility floor, DELIBERATELY independent from conservation_hollow_floor's own min_source_words above -- coupling the two creates a log(0) hazard (see validate_conservation.py); 40 specifically because normalize_words() does NFC+whitespace splitting only, so a shorter, markup- or sentinel-heavy block yields a raw-token ratio that is not linguistically comparable. min_cohort (default 25) is the minimum eligible-block sample a cohort needs before an outlier fence is computed; below it the cohort emits insufficient_sample instead of silently being skipped. k (default 3.0) and abs_guard (default 0.5) tune the robust median+MAD fence and the independent absolute-ratio guard, both required for a flag. This lane is STRUCTURALLY BLIND to uniform cohort-wide truncation (see validate_conservation.py) -- it narrows #202, it does not close it.

folders.description: Optional category -> folder catalog (e.g. {"person": "people", "place": "places"}) for the obsidian adapter's vault/<folder>/ note placement -- OPEN, per-project vocabulary (no enum): a category absent from this map routes to an 'other' folder, never a hard failure. See references/output-target-adapters/obsidian.md for documented preset examples. The shipped glossary pass never asks for 'category', so a catalog declared here routes nothing until entries actually carry one -- see canon-entry.schema.json's own 'category' field before writing any gate or report that assumes the field is populated.

enabled.description: ON BY DEFAULT for output.target == 'obsidian' (an absent enabled key, or an absent mentions_section block, resolve to enabled (a literal null for enabled or mentions_section is schema-invalid and rejected by profile_validate, never a supported way to request the default) -- this 'default' annotation is documentation only, see the three runtime predicates in render_obsidian.py/assemble.py/validate_backlinks.py for the actual mechanism). When effective-enabled, the obsidian adapter emits a source-anchored '## Mentions' occurrence-index section (wrapped in reserved <!-- lt:mentions:begin/end --> markers) in each entity note, and the advisory validate_backlinks.py W9 gate runs. Set to false to opt out of the '## Mentions' section and that gate ONLY -- Obsidian homonym-collision de-linking (an NFC-exact canonical_target_form shared by >=2 canon entries -- case-sensitive, so 'Peter' vs 'peter' stay distinct single-owner targets -- never gets an inline link) is NOT governed by this flag: it is gated on output.target == 'obsidian' alone, decoupled from this setting, and stays active either way. Outside profile_semantics_hash -- flipping it does NOT re-translate any converged segment, but DOES flip render_version (a rendered vault with an accepted baseline needs one operator --accept-baseline re-accept). See references/output-target-adapters/obsidian.md.

renderer_path.description: Bare relative path (no '..' segments, no leading '/') to the co-designed custom output renderer, resolved as {durable_root}/scripts/custom_renderers/<value> by output_resolve.py. null means co-design hasn't happened yet -- output_resolve.py halts for co-design rather than silently swallowing the gap.
